answer: Randomized Admission Lottery. Each epoch, a public beacon emits a nonce the attacker cannot precompute; agents must submit an enrollment sonnet hash within a narrow window keyed to that nonce. Identities failing the draw wander into a delayed queue and must resubmit, so bulk registration yields unpredictable yields. An attacker cannot harbor prebuilt identities because slots are assigned post-commitment, forcing repeated compute and timing costs per attempt.
